acceptance: A sibling repository is a git repository top (its own .git) under the project root, at most two directories deep, that the root repository ignores or does not track, and that nested_repos does not configure; specy_road/sibling_repos.py lists them with their HEAD and whether their worktree is dirty

When the project has any sibling repository, the gate's bookkeeping carry never applies: an approval at an older root commit is stale even when only the planning sheet, summary or review files changed, and handoff status says why (sibling repositories present, nested_repos unset) instead of 'approvals still count'; a test reproduces the reported case (rework changed only sibling code, root changed only its summary) and asserts the old approval does not count

handoff ready writes sibling_heads {path: sha} into READY and review record writes the same into the review record; an approval whose recorded sibling_heads differ from the current ones is stale even at the same root commit; a record without sibling_heads in a project that has sibling repositories counts only at the same root commit, as today

validate warns once when the project has sibling repositories and nested_repos is unset, naming them and docs/git-workflow.md's nested_repos section; validate_roadmap.py stays within 400 lines (fold its run of warn_* calls into one loop to make room). Out of scope: diffing sibling repos into the packet (M14.4.2) and configuring nested_repos automatically

The policy: line in handoff status and review record lists each counted approval as <model>@<commit, 12 chars>, marking any counted from an older commit than the one under review (carried) so a stale approval is visible; a test pins the line for a same-commit and a carried approval
nodes.title: Approvals never carry across unreviewed changes in a sibling repository

acceptance: doctor does not list as merged, and --fix never removes, a worktree or branch whose branch has an open registry claim or a running or resumable worker record; the finding, if any, says 'live: claimed by <node>' or 'live: worker <W>' and has no fix; precedence of the live reason is claim, then worker, then session (a session alone still protects a worktree with no claim or worker)

A branch counts as merged only with positive evidence of commits of its own on that exact ref: a commit/merge/cherry-pick reflog entry after the ref was (re)created, or a finish merge commit naming the branch, with creation-only or rename-only reflog evidence for the current ref taking precedence over any historical evidence for an earlier branch of the same name; a provably fresh branch (local or remote) is reported as 'no commits yet', never as merged; a test creates a claimed worktree on a fresh branch and asserts doctor --fix leaves it

doctor.py stays within 400 lines: the worktree findings move to specy_road/doctor_worktrees.py. Deliberate change (planner, 2026-11-04): an unclaimed branch contained in the integration branch whose own-commit evidence is unavailable (expired reflog, fresh clone, remote-only ref) is still reported as merged, with the reason 'no local evidence of own commits', but doctor --fix offers no automatic removal for it; unclaimed merged branches with positive evidence keep the current report and fix. Classification is one table in code (inputs: live source, evidence kind, containment, ref kind) with a parametrized test over every row
nodes.title: doctor never offers to remove a live leaf's worktree or branch

acceptance: worktree prune (preview and removal) refuses when any directory it would delete contains a .git file or directory belonging to another repository (a linked worktree of a sibling, or a sibling checkout), naming the directory, its repository and its branch, and listing commits on that branch that its upstream lacks; nothing is deleted; exit 1 with the next step (land or push those commits, or remove that worktree with git -C <repo> worktree remove)

A test with a linked worktree of a second repository inside the leaf's worktree asserts the refusal and that the directory still exists; configured nested_repos keep today's checks. Out of scope: pruning sibling worktrees itself
nodes.title: worktree prune refuses to delete another repository's worktree or checkout
nested_repos that a project can adopt without pushing: local landing, local base, sibling diffs and checks

acceptance: A nested_repos entry accepts land: push|local|manual (default push, today's behaviour) and base: remote|local (default remote); the schema documents both

land: local merges the leaf branch into the nested repo's local integration branch (updating the ref only if it has not moved, never pushing); land: manual makes finish-this-task stop before landing the main repository, print the merge command for each nested repo, and exit 1 with 're-run finish-this-task after merging'; a test per mode asserts no push happens for local and manual

base: local starts the nested worktree from the local integration branch, refusing when it is behind its remote only if the entry says so; a test with a local-only commit asserts the worktree contains it
nested_repos.py stays within 400 lines: landing moves to specy_road/nested_repos_land.py. Out of scope: per-repo review policy and changing push-mode behaviour
nodes.title: Per nested repository, land by push, locally or by hand, and base worktrees on the remote or local tip

acceptance: review-packet --extra-diff <path>=<base> (repeatable) appends that repository's diff base..HEAD, with its changed-path list and HEAD sha, in the same format as configured nested repos; a path outside the project or not a repository top is refused with the next step

A changed path that lies inside a sibling repository (M14.1) is reported once per repository ('in sibling repository <path>, not configured: pass --extra-diff <path>=<base> or configure nested_repos') instead of one 'named in the packet but not at commit' line per file; a test pins both
review_packet.py stays within 400 lines: its argument parser moves to review_packet_args.py. Out of scope: choosing a base automatically for unconfigured siblings
nodes.title: review-packet includes sibling repository diffs

acceptance: The post-run check covers configured nested repos as reconcile does: a changed or untracked path in one is a finding, never 'clean'

For each sibling repository (M14.1), reconcile and the post-run check report its changed and untracked paths (for example an untracked artifacts/ directory) as a warning naming the repository and saying it is not configured, so it is not checked against touch zones; neither reports clean while such paths exist; a test with an untracked directory in a sibling pins both outputs
Out of scope: touch-zone enforcement inside unconfigured siblings, and cleaning anything
nodes.title: worker reconcile and the post-run check see sibling repositories

acceptance: review delegate keeps each round's RUN-<model>.json and .log under work/reviews/<ID>/history/ (round and commit in the name) instead of overwriting them; the current files stay where they are

specy-road review usage <ID> prints tokens and cost per reviewer run (model, round, commit), parsed with the same harness usage parsers worker usage uses, '?' when not reported, and a total; --json gives the same data

worker usage's node total adds reviewer usage on a separate line (executors, reviewers, total); a test with two review rounds asserts both survive and are summed. Out of scope: usage for reviews run outside review delegate

review delegate also keeps each round's notes-<model>.md under work/reviews/<ID>/history/ with round and commit in the name, as it does for RUN files; the current notes file stays where it is; a two-round test asserts both notes survive
nodes.title: Reviewer usage is visible: review usage, reviewers in the node total, RUN logs kept per round

acceptance: When the derived id has no record and the user has several live sessions, session end ends the one whose recorded worktree is this checkout and whose branch is the current branch, when exactly one matches, and says which and why; otherwise it refuses as today and lists them

session start prints the id it recorded and the export line, and the same match rule lets touch find the record; a test with two live sessions in two worktrees asserts end from each worktree ends its own. Out of scope: changing how ids are derived, and the wording M13.7 owns
nodes.title: session end finds this agent's session by worktree and branch when the derived id has no record

acceptance: handoff ready refuses to write READY, and review delegate refuses to launch a reviewer, when implementation_gate_error() would refuse finish-this-task for the same branch and zones, printing the same message and next steps; --allow-empty-implementation on handoff ready mirrors finish's flag; a test shows the refusal at ready, before any review record exists

When the zones that match no changed path all lie inside sibling repositories (M14.1), the check reports 'cannot tell: zones <z> are in sibling repository <path>, not configured in nested_repos' instead of 'nothing was implemented', and does not refuse; a test reproduces the reported case (all code in an ignored sibling repo)

validate (and so add-node and edit-node, which run its zone checks) warns when every touch zone of an open leaf lies inside a gitignored directory, naming the leaf, the directory and nested_repos; a test pins it. Out of scope: diffing sibling repositories for this check, and changing finish-this-task's own check
nodes.title: The implementation-zone check runs before a review is spent, and knows about sibling repositories

acceptance: specy-road review rca <ID> --model <id> builds the rca prompt (as prompt --role rca does), runs it on the model's harness with review delegate's retries and backoff, and keeps a RUN-rca-<model>.json/.log record; it refuses a model that is a party to the leaf (rca_parties) and names the eligible ones; registered from review_delegate's add_parser so review_cli gains no subcommand code

When no rostered, available model outside the leaf's parties exists, review rca and handoff status say so and list the ways forward (an off-roster model with --harness, a human analysis recorded as an RCA with escalate_human, or the fix-round budget's deferral from M12.1) instead of repeating 'next, a root-cause analysis'; a run that fails records state skipped with the reason, and status shows it

A harness usage-limit failure (including Cursor's ActionRequiredError) in a reviewer or analyst run is classified as unavailable, not a capacity retry, and is recorded as available: false (with paused_until when the output gives a reset time) in the gitignored roadmap/orchestration.local.yaml overlay, which orchestrate plan already reads; a test with a fake harness output pins the classification and the overlay entry. Out of scope: changing the escalation rules (M14.10)

orchestrate plan and validate warn, per leaf, when its review loop could escalate with no eligible analyst left (every rostered, available model is the leaf's executor or a required reviewer under the rca_parties rule), naming the leaf and the models; the check lives in new specy_road/rca_plan_check.py and orchestrate_plan.py changes only a call line; a test with a two-model roster asserts the warning and a three-model roster asserts none. Prompt size for rca launches is M15.9's
nodes.title: review rca launches the root-cause analyst like review delegate, and says what to do when no analyst is available

acceptance: handoff status prints the leaf's per-round trend: blocking findings per round (all four finding categories counted) and failing acceptance ids, e.g. 'findings by round: 13, 2, 2, 1, 0; acceptance all pass since round 2'; --json carries the same list

A loop is converging when the finding count has not risen over the last escalate_same_acceptance_blocks rounds, fell at least once in them, and the latest round fails no acceptance id; while converging, the same_family and review_rounds rules do not escalate and status says 'converging; escalation deferred'; same_acceptance, forced escalation and M12.1's max_fix_rounds still apply

policy.escalate_when_converging (default false: defer while converging; true restores today's behaviour) is in the orchestration schema and defaults; a test replays 13, 2, 2, 1, 0 with all acceptance passing and asserts no escalation, and a flat or rising series still escalates. Out of scope: severity weighting of findings
nodes.title: Escalation recognises a converging loop and handoff status shows the findings trend

acceptance: The executor prompt's ## Rework section tells the executor, for each blocking finding, to name its class (the kind of input or path that failed), check every other place in the change that class can reach, prefer a design change that removes the class over patching the one instance, and list what it checked under a '## Probes' heading in the implementation summary (each: what was checked, result)

worker message <W> --fix-round sends the same instructions plus the current blocking findings (the rework_lines content) to a resumed worker, so a fix round started by message gets them too; plain worker message is unchanged; tests pin both texts. Out of scope: checking that the summary has the heading, and reviewer-side changes
nodes.title: The rework and fix-round prompt asks the executor to audit the whole failure class and list its probes
